sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Mg–Si binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset MgSi-12Sch.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L → Mg2Si + (Si), lies at 939.3 °C.
The Mg–Si system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as congruent compound, simple eutectic.

The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of M. Schick, B. Hallstedt, A. Glensk, B. Grabowski, T. Hickel, M. Hampl, J. Groebner, J. Neugebauer, R. Schmid-Fetzer, Calphad, 37, 77-86(2012). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
The melting point of Mg reproduced by the dataset is 652.1 °C.
At 939.3 °C the eutectic L → Mg2Si + (Si) takes place; the L phase then contains 54.3 at.%.
The eutectic reaction L → (Mg) + Mg2Si is calculated at 637.1 °C, with L at 1.5 at.% Si.
Mg2Si melts congruently at 1077.4 °C and 33.3 at.% Si.
According to Table 2, Mg2Si remains stable up to 1077.4 °C (congruent melting).
At 1750 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −16345 J/mol, at 48.0 at.% Si.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of Mg2Si at 298.15 K is −21.05 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
Its heat capacity at room temperature is 22.92 J/(mol K).
For the equiatomic liquid at 1750 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −19.16 kJ/mol.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
